sentences.zh: 说他们曾身处，嗯，你知道的，一个成长到 Swift 般成熟度如此之快的语言的真正起点。

sentences.en: Um, and, uh, yeah, so, so maybe, so maybe tell us a little bit about, about your experience with, uh, with Swift.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且，呃，是的，所以，所以也许，所以也许跟我们讲讲你关于，呃，关于 Swift 的经历。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, it was a, it was a, uh, once in a lifetime opportunity for somebody who's interested in language design, you know, because, uh,
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个，这是一个，对于对语言设计感兴趣的人来说千载难逢的机会，你知道的，因为，呃，

sentences.en: uh, languages do come along every week and they die in obscurity.
sentences.zh: 呃，语言每周都在出现，然后又在默默无闻中消亡。

sentences.en: So, uh, you know, uh, so if you've been around a few years and, and seen this, you only want to get engaged in a, uh, in a language project.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，呃，如果你在这个圈子里待了几年，并见证了这一点，你只会想参与到一个，呃，语言项目中。

sentences.en: If you think it's really got some legs and, uh, you know, this one had, uh, Apple's future behind it.
sentences.zh: 如果你认为它真的很有发展前景，而且，你知道的，这个项目有苹果的未来作为后盾。

sentences.en: Apple was staking its future on it, although to what extent wasn't entirely clear at the, in the early days.
sentences.zh: 苹果把它的未来押在了上面，尽管在早期，这种押注的程度并不是完全清晰的。

sentences.en: Um, uh, and it had an amazing group of, of people, uh, that I had faith in, you know, starting with Doug Gregor, who was my close friend.
sentences.zh: 嗯，呃，它有一群了不起的人，呃，是我有信心的，从我的密友道格·格雷戈尔开始。

sentences.en: Um, and, uh, yeah, so what was it like?
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且，呃，是的，那是什么感觉？

sentences.en: It was, uh, it was a thrilling adventure.
sentences.zh: 它是一个，这是一场惊心动魄的冒险。

sentences.en: Um, you know, um, there, it was, you know, it was scrappy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，嗯，那里，它，你知道的，它是充满干劲的。

sentences.en: We had a group of about 10 to 12, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我们有一群大约 10 到 12 人，我想。

sentences.en: Uh, that maybe wasn't even the, the starting size might've been, might've been like eight.
sentences.zh: 呃，那可能甚至都不是起始规模，可能只有，可能只有大约 8 个人。

sentences.en: Um, but, uh, you know, we, Chris, uh, Latner to his credit, uh, ran the, ran the thing very much by consensus as much as possible.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但是，你知道的，我们，克里斯·拉特纳值得称赞的是，他尽可能地通过共识来管理这件事。

sentences.en: Um, and, uh, and while, you know, some people denigrate design by committee, I have always found that the, the process of coming to consensus, uh, inside of the C++ committee,
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且，呃，虽然，你知道的，有些人贬低委员会设计，但我一直发现，达成共识的过程，呃，比如在 C++ 委员会内部，

sentences.en: for example, has been more beneficial than, than harmful.
sentences.zh: 一直以来都是利大于弊的。

sentences.en: Um, and so we had a lot of fights about things.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以我们为很多事情进行了争论。

sentences.en: Um, uh, we all learned a lot from each other.
sentences.zh: 嗯，呃，我们都从彼此身上学到了很多东西。

sentences.en: There was an amazing amount of, uh, of different experiences in the group.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这个团队里有着惊人数量的、各种各样的不同经验。

sentences.en: Um, yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对。

sentences.en: And, and it was, it was a thrill, but when I got there, the, the language was, uh, extremely immature.
sentences.zh: 而且，而且这真的，这很让人兴奋，但当我到那儿时，呃，那门语言非常不成熟。

sentences.en: It was almost impossible to build anything generic, um, with it.
sentences.zh: 用它几乎不可能构建出任何通用的东西，呃。

sentences.en: And, and, uh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 而且，而且，呃，对。

sentences.en: So, so the first, the first few months, I would say were quite frustrating because of that.
sentences.zh: 所以，所以前，前几个月，我可以说因为这个而相当沮丧。

sentences.en: It was, it made it really hard to make progress and, you know, it was good to be part of the design discussions and, and move the design forward.
sentences.zh: 这，这真的很难取得进展，而且，你知道的，能参与设计讨论并推动设计向前发展是很好的。

sentences.en: So that was great.
sentences.zh: 所以那真的很棒。

sentences.en: But like, I was also responsible for the standard library and how do you build a standard library on a fragile foundation that barely works?
sentences.zh: 但就像，我也负责标准库，你怎么能在几乎无法正常工作的脆弱基础之上构建标准库呢？

sentences.en: Um, uh, and, uh, at some point, uh, you know, the, the pressure of not delivering anything became too much for me.
sentences.zh: 嗯，呃，而且，呃，在某个时候，你知道的，未能交付任何成果的压力对我来说变得太大了。

sentences.en: And I, and I decided, okay, I'm just going to do what I, what I have always done with broken C++ compilers, which is figure out how to, you know,
sentences.zh: 然后我，然后我决定，好吧，我打算做我，我一直对坏掉的 C++ 编译器做的事情，那就是弄清楚怎么，你知道的，

sentences.en: coerce them into doing what I need.
sentences.zh: 强迫它们做我需要的事。

sentences.en: And, um, who cares if it's, if it's beautiful or, or even correct.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，谁在乎它是不是，是不是漂亮，甚至是不是正确。

sentences.en: You know, um, so that got me over a hump when I was first able to build an array, that was, that was something.
sentences.zh: 你知道，嗯，所以这帮我度过了一个难关，当我第一次能够构建一个数组时，那，那可真了不起。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, I, I guess, I guess it really is early days of building an array is, uh, you know, is, is a challenge, but, uh, and, and,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我，我想，我想构建数组的早期阶段确实是，你知道的，是一个挑战，但是，呃，而且，而且，

sentences.en: and you were involved a bit in the design of C++ of, of, of Swift's, um, generic system.
sentences.zh: 而且你多多少少参与了 C++ 的，呃，Swift 的泛型系统的设计。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: A bit.
sentences.zh: 一点点。

sentences.en: Um, uh, yeah, definitely.
sentences.zh: 嗯，呃，对，绝对的。

sentences.en: I, I had some influences, especially later on.
sentences.zh: 我，我有过一些影响，特别是在后期。

sentences.en: I would say that the, a lot of the inspiration for the initial, uh, design of the generic system came from work that Jeremy Seek had done on something called system G, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想说，泛型系统最初设计的很多灵感，来自于杰里米·西克（Jeremy Seek）在某个叫系统 G 的东西上做过的工作，我想是的。

sentences.en: Um, and, uh, basically what he was doing as far as I understand.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且，呃，基本上据我所知他当时在做的是。

sentences.en: It was building, uh, a generic system with separate compilation.
sentences.zh: 它正在构建一个带有独立编译的泛型系统。

sentences.en: Um, and in the, in the sense that Haskell does it, except with associated types, which at least standard Haskell doesn't have.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在 Haskell 的那种意义上，除了带有关联类型，至少标准 Haskell 是没有关联类型的。

sentences.en: Um, and, uh, and I think Doug took that as, as a foundation.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且，呃，而且我认为道格（Doug）把那个作为了基础。

sentences.en: And part of the reason that was so important at Apple was, um, or for Swift was that Swift needed to, uh, needed to,
sentences.zh: 在苹果公司，之所以这如此重要的一部分原因，呃，或者对 Swift 来说是，Swift 需要，呃，需要，

sentences.en: to not lose the one really killer quality that Objective-C had for Apple, which is this ability to upgrade either side of, of an interface without breaking code.
sentences.zh: 不能失去 Objective-C 对苹果来说真正具有的那个杀手级特质，也就是在不破坏代码的情况下升级接口任意一侧的能力。

sentences.en: So, and, and without recompiling.
sentences.zh: 所以，而且，呃，不需要重新编译。

sentences.en: A, a, a, a, a challenge that continues to plague the C++ ecosystem and the evolution of C++.
sentences.zh: 这，这是一个继续困扰 C++ 生态系统以及 C++ 演进的挑战。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So that, that's what they called, uh, uh, resilience or ABI resilience.
sentences.zh: 所以这，这就是他们所谓的，呃，呃，韧性或 ABI 韧性。

sentences.en: Um, and, uh, and so to do that, you have to be able to separately compile generics into something that doesn't change when you, when you invoke them with different, you know, uh,
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且，呃，所以要做到这一点，你必须能够将泛型独立编译成这样一种东西：当你用不同的，你知道的，呃，

sentences.en: parameter types.
sentences.zh: 参数类型调用它们时，它不会改变。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And I mean, I, I think, I think this, you know, the, this part of Swift is a really good example of, you know, we, we, we have to,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为，我认为这个，你知道的，Swift 的这部分是一个非常好的例子，你知道的，我们，我们，我们不得不，

sentences.en: we have some talk in C++ about like the ABI problem.
sentences.zh: 我们在 C++ 中讨论过一些关于诸如 ABI 问题的事情。

sentences.en: And some people are like, well, we should just go and, you know, break ABI or, you know, not break ABI.
sentences.zh: 有些人觉得，嗯，我们应该直接去，你知道的，打破 ABI，或者，你知道的，不打破 ABI。

sentences.en: And it's almost, the, the conversation is usually one that makes it seem like it's simply a policy question.
sentences.zh: 而且几乎，这种对话通常会让人觉得这仅仅是一个政策问题。

sentences.en: Um, to me, it's never, it's always seemed like there's been a missing discussion about the technical, uh, limitations that we have that, you know, we don't really,
sentences.zh: 对我来说，从来都不是这样，总是感觉好像缺少了一场关于我们拥有的技术，呃，局限性的讨论，你知道的，我们并不是真的，

sentences.en: it's not something that was, the language was designed for from the ground up.
sentences.zh: 这不是那种从底层开始就为之设计的语言特性。

sentences.en: Um, and who knows, maybe, maybe it's not too late to bring some sort of resiliency to C++.
sentences.zh: 嗯，谁知道呢，也许，也许现在为 C++ 引入某种韧性还不算太晚。

sentences.en: Um, but, uh, I think it's much easier, of course, if you design it from the start of your language.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但是，呃，当然，如果你从语言之初就设计它，我认为要容易得多。

sentences.en: Um, you know, one of the problems that would come from almost any form of resiliency that we'd add to C++ is, would it have some cost over doing things, the non-resilient ways?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，我们将任何形式的韧性添加到 C++ 中所带来的问题之一就是，相比于不具备韧性的做法，它会不会有一些成本？

sentences.en: And if it did have some costs, then how would you get people to, to buy into using it?
sentences.zh: 如果它确实有一些成本，那么你如何让人们接受并使用它呢？

sentences.en: And, uh, one, one of the problems of course, is that some people who are making the choices that will, that will impact whether or not you can change your ABI,
sentences.zh: 而且，呃，当然，问题之一是，一些做出选择的人，这些选择将影响你是否能够更改你的 ABI，

sentences.en: they may not realize when they're writing their code that they needed resiliency.
sentences.zh: 他们在编写代码时可能并没有意识到他们需要韧性。

sentences.en: Uh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 呃，对。

sentences.en: Um, so, all of these things are, are real problems for, for Swift too.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，对 Swift 来说，所有这些也都是真正的问题。

sentences.en: I mean, uh, uh, ABI resilience at generic boundaries is, is a definite performance coSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，呃，呃，泛型边界处的 ABI 韧性确实是一个性能成本。

sentences.en: Because what it means is that you end up with some kind of dynamic dispatch, even though it's static polymorphism,
sentences.zh: 因为这意味着你最终会使用某种动态分发，尽管它是静态多态，

sentences.en: you end up with functionally like, like, uh, implementation in the implementation, a dynamic dispatch that, that chooses one implementation or another based on the,
sentences.zh: 你在功能上最终会得到，就像，呃，在实现中，一种动态分发，它根据，

sentences.en: on the input types.
sentences.zh: 根据输入类型来选择某一种实现。

sentences.en: Now, one thing you can do to, to, um, mitigate some of that is to, is to have a JIT, right?
sentences.zh: 现在，你可以做的一件用来，呃，缓解其中一部分问题的事情是，拥有一个 JIT，对吧？

sentences.en: Uh, or a, or some kind of late recompilation that, that erases the cost at the resilience boundaries.
sentences.zh: 呃，或者某种延迟重新编译，从而消除韧性边界处的成本。

sentences.en: But regardless, you, you, you have to think of it, every resilience boundary with polymorphism behind it, even static polymorphism as a virtual function call.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，你，你，你必须这样看待它：每一个背后有多态性（甚至是静态多态性）的韧性边界，都像是一次虚函数调用。

sentences.en: And, and, and, you know, one of the things that,
sentences.zh: 而且，而且，而且，你知道的，其中一件事，

sentences.en: that generic programming depends on being able to hide very small operations like the increment of an integer or a pointer behind an abstraction boundary.
sentences.zh: 泛型编程依赖于将非常小的操作（例如整型或指针的自增）隐藏在抽象边界之后的能力。

sentences.en: The, you know, the, you know, whatever the, uh, the concept requirement is in C++ terMs.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，用 C++ 术语来说，无论概念要求是什么。

sentences.en: Um, and so, you, you know, when you, when you pay the cost of a dynamic dispatch for tiny operations, your code gets a lot slower.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，你，你知道的，当你为微小操作支付动态分发的成本时，你的代码会变得慢得多。

sentences.en: So there are all of these, uh, these halfway points that you can get into in, with Swift, uh, with regards to, uh, to things like saying that this thing is in lineable.
sentences.zh: 所以，在 Swift 中，关于诸如声明某个东西是内联的（inlinable）之类的事情，你可以进入所有这些，呃，这些折中点。

sentences.en: If you say it's in lineable, then the resilience boundary goes away, but then again, you can't change it.
sentences.zh: 如果你说它是内联的，那么韧性边界就消失了，但话又说回来，你就无法更改它了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And, and I think, yeah, I think the whole question of library evolution is something, uh, Swift hasn't yet really, uh, addressed.
sentences.zh: 而且，而且我认为，对，我认为关于库演进的整个问题，呃，Swift 还没有真正解决。

sentences.en: Um, it's addressed, um, it's addressed the problem of how do you build an ABI so that you can extend a struct without breaking code.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它解决了，嗯，它解决了如何构建 ABI 的问题，以便你可以扩展结构体而不破坏代码。

sentences.en: Um, but what are like, there's a whole, there's a whole universe, I think of tools and, and processes that, that library developers need to have in order to be able to,
sentences.zh: 嗯，但是，有什么呢，我认为库开发者需要有一整套工具和流程，以便能够，

sentences.en: to effectively evolve their libraries, which I don't think, I don't think Swift has done anything to actually dig into yet.
sentences.zh: 有效地演进他们的库，而我认为 Swift 还没有做任何真正深入探讨这方面的工作。

sentences.en: But they've had a lot of other stuff on their plate.
sentences.zh: 但他们手头还有很多其他的事情要忙。

sentences.en: I was going to say, is there a language that you think is the good archetypal model for those kinds of tools or?
sentences.zh: 我正想说，你认为有没有哪门语言是这类工具的良好原型模型？

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 哦，没有。

sentences.en: Uh, I don't, I don't think, I don't, as far as I know, nobody has really tried to figure that out.
sentences.zh: 呃，我不知道，我不认为，据我所知，没有人真正试图去弄清楚这一点。

sentences.en: Um, and, you know, I think, I think starting with, with the ability to create ABI resilience is, um, is important.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且，你知道，我认为，从具备创建 ABI 韧性的能力开始，呃，是很重要的。

sentences.en: Uh, so I think Swift is in a unique position, at least of, of having that as a platform.
sentences.zh: 呃，所以我认为 Swift 处于一个独特的位置，至少拥有这样一个平台作为基础。

sentences.en: Um, but, uh, yeah, um, I think there's a lot of work left to do.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但是，呃，是的，呃，我认为还有很多工作要做。

sentences.en: I mean, yeah, a lot of, a lot of languages, including a lot of new languages, you know, struggle with this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对，很多语言，包括很多新语言，你知道的，都在为此苦恼。

sentences.en: I know that right now in the Rust world, there's a lot of conversations going on about ABI, um, uh, resiliency.
sentences.zh: 我知道现在在 Rust 社区中，有很多关于 ABI，呃，韧性的讨论。

sentences.en: And, um, uh, I'm going to badly summarize my understanding, which is that for a long time, the model in Rust had essentially been, we were not, you know, we don't provide,
sentences.zh: 而且，呃，我将糟糕地总结一下我的理解，那就是长期以来，Rust 中的模型本质上是，我们没有，你知道的，我们不提供，

sentences.en: or we don't worry about ABI stability.
sentences.zh: 或者我们不担心 ABI 稳定性。

sentences.en: And now there's maybe some question that, or there's some, there's some folks who might, uh, uh, want that.
sentences.zh: 而现在可能有一些疑问，或者有一些人，呃，可能会想要这个。

sentences.en: And they're trying to sort out how exactly would they do that, especially in a world where they sort of, you know, they sort of statically build everything.
sentences.zh: 他们正在摸索究竟该如何做到这一点，特别是在他们那种基本上，你知道的，静态构建一切的世界里。

sentences.en: Um, yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对。

sentences.en: Um, yeah, well, one interesting answer for, for performance oriented languages like C++ and Rust is,
sentences.zh: 嗯，好吧，对于像 C++ 和 Rust 这样的注重性能的语言来说，一个有趣的答案是，

sentences.en: is tell people how to build APIs that can be extended and give them some guarantees, but, but don't, uh, don't make that the default.
sentences.zh: 告诉人们如何构建可以被扩展的 API 并给予他们一些保证，但是，但是，不要把它作为默认设置。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So there are things that we do in C++ all the time, uh, which we get from C, you know, you build a C interface, you, you dynamically allocate your struct,
sentences.zh: 所以有些事情我们在 C++ 中一直在做，呃，这些是从 C 那里继承来的，你知道的，你构建一个 C 接口，你动态分配你的结构体，

sentences.en: then you can extend the struct anytime you want.
sentences.zh: 然后你随时可以扩展该结构体。

sentences.en: Those kinds of techniques actually work in practice to some extent.
sentences.zh: 这些技术在实践中确实在一定程度上起作用。

sentences.en: And they, they, parts of them may be guaranteed.
sentences.zh: 而且它们，它们的一部分可能是受到保证的。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But yeah, like a good example of this in C++, which is, um, would be like stood mutex.
sentences.zh: 但是，对，就像 C++ 中一个很好的例子，呃，就是 std::mutex。

sentences.en: So on, um, on MSVC, their stood mutex implementation is like, it, it's eight, it's 10 times larger than their stood shared mutex.
sentences.zh: 所以，在，呃，在 MSVC 上，他们的 std::mutex 实现就像是，它，它比他们的 std::shared_mutex 大 8 倍、10 倍。

sentences.en: And it's like two times slower.
sentences.zh: 而且它慢了两倍。

sentences.en: And the reason is because their stood mutex has to be, be ABI compatible back to like the windows XP mutex layout, which is like this huge thing that uses this very old API.
sentences.zh: 原因在于他们的 std::mutex 必须向后保持 ABI 兼容，一直兼容到 Windows XP 的 mutex 布局，那是一个使用非常古老 API 的庞然大物。

sentences.en: And, um, you know, fortunately no one should ever use a mutex.
sentences.zh: 而且，呃，你知道，幸好根本没有人应该去使用 mutex。

sentences.en: So, yeah, but, but, you know, it, it would have been a fairly simple thing to avoid this problem.
sentences.zh: 所以，对，但是，你知道，避免这个问题其实是一件相当简单的事情。

sentences.en: If they had just, instead of having the, the, the, um, you know, the, the metadata for that mutex be, uh, just regular data members of stood mutex,
sentences.zh: 如果他们当时只是，而不是把，把，呃，你知道的，那个 mutex 的元数据做成 std::mutex 的常规数据成员，

sentences.en: they could have just put it in some opaque struct and just had a pointer to it.
sentences.zh: 他们完全可以把它放在某个不透明的结构体里，然后放一个指向它的指针就行了。

sentences.en: It's just that when they did their implementation, they didn't, um, they didn't make that decision.
sentences.zh: 只是当他们进行实现时，他们没有，呃，没有做出那个决定。

sentences.en: And there was, you know, there was a trade-off to that at another level of indirection.
sentences.zh: 而且你知道的，在另一个间接层级上，这需要做出权衡。

sentences.en: Um, but, uh, I think it's something that we perhaps should have designed for more consciously when we, uh, when we first started standardizing C++.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但是，呃，我认为在我们，呃，最初开始标准化 C++ 时，这可能是我们应该更有意识地去设计的事情。

sentences.en: Um, yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Uh, well, I mean, that's, that's up to each individual implementation, right?
sentences.zh: 呃，好吧，我的意思是，那是每个具体实现自己的事，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Um, were you, were you around when the, um, when the infamous stood string ABI break, um, came through the committee?
sentences.zh: 嗯，当那个，呃，当那个声名狼藉的 std::string ABI 破坏，呃，通过委员会的时候，你在场吗？

sentences.en: Uh, I, I'm not familiar with this story.
sentences.zh: 呃，我对这个故事不熟悉。

sentences.en: So, uh, at least not in those terMs.
sentences.zh: 所以，呃，至少不是用那些术语。

sentences.en: This, this was, um, so in C++11, we, we changed some of the complexity guarantees on stood string in such a way that it,
sentences.zh: 这是，呃，所以在 C++11 中，我们修改了 std::string 的一些复杂度保证，以至于它，

sentences.en: it prohibited the GCC copy on write implementation from conforming to what stood string was.
sentences.zh: 它使得 GCC 的写时复制（copy-on-write）实现无法符合 std::string 的规范。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，对。

sentences.en: I think I remember, I think I remember lots of complaints about the, about the, at that time,
sentences.zh: 我想我记得，我想我记得当时有很多关于，关于那个的抱怨，

sentences.en: I think I remember people saying that you couldn't actually make a copy on write implementation conform.
sentences.zh: 我想我记得人们说你实际上无法让写时复制实现符合规范。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: It, what, what, what's interesting to me is that, uh, everybody who I've ever talked to from that era doesn't remember it as being a,
sentences.zh: 令我感兴趣的是，呃，我交谈过的那个时代的所有人，

sentences.en: a controversial thing at the time that the requirements were changed.
sentences.zh: 在修改要求的时候，都不觉得这是一件有争议的事情。

sentences.en: It was only afterwards that we realized how significant, uh, of a change it was and the impacts that it had on the GCC implementation.
sentences.zh: 直到后来我们才意识到这是一个多么重大的，呃，改变，以及它对 GCC 实现产生的影响。

sentences.en: And, uh, you know, there, there's, there's some folks that, including myself, that think that it's, it ended up slowing down adoption of C++11.
sentences.zh: 而且，呃，你知道，有一些人，包括我自己，认为它最终拖慢了 C++11 的普及。

sentences.en: Um, because, uh, if you upgraded to C++11 to the, you know, the compliance C++11 stood string, uh, it would, you know,
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为，呃，如果你升级到 C++11，升级到，你知道的，符合规范的 C++11 std::string，它会，你知道的，

sentences.en: it would be an ABI break and stood string gets used everywhere.
sentences.zh: 这将是一次 ABI 破坏，而 std::string 到处都在使用。

sentences.en: Um, and I think it's just, you know, it's, uh, we would never today in the committee,
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且我认为这只是，呃，今天在委员会中，我们绝不会，

sentences.en: we would never make such a change because we've become super sensitive to ABI changes to the degree that almost any proposal that would in some way, shape or form break ABI is,
sentences.zh: 我们绝不会做出这样的改变，因为我们对 ABI 变化变得超级敏感，以至于几乎任何在某种程度上会破坏 ABI 的提案，

sentences.en: is a non-starter.
sentences.zh: 都是根本不可行的。

sentences.en: Um, but, you know, it wasn't always that way.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但是，你知道，以前可不是这样的。

sentences.en: Um, we just didn't know, we didn't realize what the costs were at the time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们只是不知道，当时没有意识到代价是什么。

sentences.en: Well, at least, I mean, uh, to, to your credit now, I guess at least there's some consensus about, about what's important.
sentences.zh: 好吧，至少，我的意思是，呃，归功于你们，我想现在至少对什么才是重要的达成了一些共识。

sentences.en: Um, all right, uh, I mean, uh, I think at the time that ABI break happened, it was, it was fairly random.
sentences.zh: 好的，呃，我的意思是，呃，我想在那个 ABI 破坏发生的时候，它相当随机。

sentences.en: We would break, we were willing to break ABI over here, not over there for what reasons, you know, there was, there was no, uh, uh, sense of what the scale of, uh, values was.
sentences.zh: 我们会在这里破坏 ABI，不在那里破坏 ABI，出于什么原因，你知道的，根本没有，呃，对价值规模的感知。

sentences.en: Um, so, but I, I do think that, that, uh, you know, an unwillingness to break the ABI of C++ is, is a, probably a serious limitation on it being, you know,
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，但我确实认为，呃，你知道的，不愿意破坏 C++ 的 ABI，可能对它，你知道的，

sentences.en: evolving into a better language.
sentences.zh: 演进为一门更好的语言是一个严重的限制。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, I, I think it does still remain sort of an existential, um, the existential struggle and question of the C++ library evolution.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我，我认为这仍然某种程度上是 C++ 库演进中生死攸关的，呃，生死攸关的挣扎和问题。

sentences.en: Um, because, uh, as long as we live in a world where we cannot fix our mistakes after we ship them, that, that will make the committee very,
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为，呃，只要我们生活在一个发布错误后无法修复的世界里，这就会让委员会变得非常，

sentences.en: very cautious about what things we ship.
sentences.zh: 非常谨慎地对待我们发布的每一个东西。

sentences.en: Um, and so I think that the standard library will roughly continue being the same size, size and scope as it is today.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以我认为标准库的大致规模和范围将继续保持和今天差不多。

sentences.en: Um, uh, because any sort of massive expansion would bring, you know, a degree of risk that would just be unacceptable.
sentences.zh: 嗯，呃，因为任何形式的大规模扩展都会带来，你知道的，完全不可接受的风险程度。

sentences.en: Um, and so it's like, we, we, we, we all understand the rules or not rules.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以这就好像，我们，我们，大家都理解规则，或者说不是规则。

sentences.en: We all understand the, the current, you know, policies and consensus, um, and like the implications of that today.
sentences.zh: 我们都理解当前的，你知道的，政策和共识，嗯，以及今天这意味着什么。

sentences.en: Um, but I think just because we, we understand that it doesn't necessarily mean that the outcomes are the beSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但我认为，仅仅因为我们理解了这一点，并不一定意味着结果就是最好的。

sentences.en: Um, well, why can't you just, uh, standardized library components that are, are designed with resilience in mind?
sentences.zh: 嗯，为什么你们就不能，呃，把那些在设计时就考虑了韧性的库组件标准化呢？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And I, and I think that's something that we need to, um, uh, be doing.
sentences.zh: 而且我，我认为这是我们需要，呃，去做的事情。

sentences.en: Uh, but, uh, it's, it's not an area that we've really treaded into.
sentences.zh: 呃，但是，呃，这不是我们真正涉足过的领域。

sentences.en: And I think that oftentimes there's the performance trade-off and, um, yeah, but not often, always, but, but you have to, if you want the resiliency,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为通常存在性能权衡，嗯，是的，但不是通常，是一直都有，但是你必须，如果你想要韧性，

sentences.en: you have to be willing to make that trade-off.
sentences.zh: 你就必须愿意做出这种权衡。

sentences.en: Like, uh, you know, one example, um, there's been a lot of talk recently in the C++ about standardizing, um, networking.
sentences.zh: 比如，嗯，你知道，举个例子，嗯，最近在C++领域有很多关于标准化，嗯，网络功能的讨论。

sentences.en: And, uh, one question that always comes up is if we standardize some sort of secure network in some sort of TLS layer, well,
sentences.zh: 然后，嗯，经常出现的一个问题是，如果我们把某种安全的网络和某种TLS层进行标准化，那么，

sentences.en: of course that would need to be standardized in a way where we would be able to roll out, you know, security fixes, um, and deprecate old, you know, protocols, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 当然，这需要以一种能够让我们推出，你知道的，安全修复，嗯，以及废弃旧的，你知道的，协议等等的方式来进行标准化。

sentences.en: Um, and I mean, I think we could do it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，我觉得我们能做到。

sentences.en: I think that if we sat down and if we said from the start,
sentences.zh: 我觉得如果我们坐下来，如果我们从一开始就说，

sentences.en: hey, this library component needs to be something that's going to be resilient to change, we could design it in that way.
sentences.zh: 嘿，这个库组件必须具备能够适应变化的能力，我们就能以这种方式设计它。

sentences.en: There might be some, some performance trade-offs, but it could be done.
sentences.zh: 可能会有一些，一些性能上的权衡，但这是可以做到的。

sentences.en: Um, and I think that oftentimes the conversation in the C++ committee has just been, well, this is an ABI break, so we can't do it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且我认为C++委员会里的讨论往往只是，好吧，这是一个ABI破坏，所以我们做不到。

sentences.en: And we maybe need to have more of the conversation of, you know, how could we build, you know, this new component to be resilient.
sentences.zh: 也许我们需要更多地去讨论，你知道的，我们如何才能构建，你知道的，这个新组件使其具有适应性。

sentences.en: Makes sense.
sentences.zh: 有道理。

sentences.en: Thanks for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听。

sentences.en: We hope you enjoyed and have a great day.
sentences.zh: 希望你喜欢，祝你今天过得愉快。
